intended_object: The Dynkin system (λ-system) generated by a collection s of subsets of α: the smallest family that contains s and ∅, and is closed under complements and countable disjoint unions. Taken from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The definition uses the inductive predicate `GenerateHas s`. Its constructors are: the basic sets in s, the empty set, closure under complement, and closure under countable unions of pairwise disjoint sequences indexed by ℕ. These are exactly the axioms of `DynkinSystem`. An inductive predicate is the least predicate closed under its constructors, so this is the least Dynkin system containing s, i.e. the intersection of all Dynkin systems containing s. That is the standard generated λ-system. Nothing in the construction needs extra structure on α, so it is stated in full generality. It also matches how Mathlib builds generated σ-algebras (`MeasurableSpace.generateFrom` via `GenerateMeasurable`). This is Mathlib's own definition of the notion, so there is no separate counterpart to cite.
